        raise ValueError('Distinct before/after builds are required')

        print(json.dumps({'validated': True, 'core_plan': plan,

                          'C_reference_remeasured': False, 'processes': 12}, indent=2))

    args.output.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=False)

    for key in ['GOMAXPROCS', 'PPROF']:
        env.pop(key, None)
    compiler = compiler_snapshot()
    started = datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat()
    load_start = list(os.getloadavg())
    commands = [
        [sys.executable, '-B', str(ROOT / 'bin/benchmark/measure.py'), '--plan',
         str(args.output / 'core-plan.json'), '--output', str(args.output / 'core')],
        [sys.executable, '-B', str(Path(__file__).with_name('collect-all.py')), '--before',
         frozen['go_before_all']['directory'], '--after', str(args.after_all.resolve()),
         '--output', str(args.output / 'all')],
    ]
    for command in commands:
        verify_freeze(frozen)
        C['verify_hashes'](compiler['files_sha256'])
        subprocess.run(command, cwd=ROOT, env=env, check=True)
        verify_freeze(frozen)
        C['verify_hashes'](compiler['files_sha256'])
    core = json.loads((args.output / 'core/results.json').read_text())
    all_cases = json.loads((args.output / 'all/results.json').read_text())
    labels = C['ROWS']
    core_times = {variant: dict(zip(labels, data['times_us'])) for variant, data in core.items()}
    core_aggregates = {variant: metrics(times, frozen['c_times_us']) for variant, times in core_times.items()}
    core_historical = metrics(frozen['historical_go_core_times_us'], frozen['c_times_us'])
    for key, value in core_historical.items():
        if not math.isclose(value, frozen['historical_aggregates'][key], rel_tol=1e-12):
            raise ValueError('Historical metrics do not reproduce the official archive')

    # for library23 only. Both sides of every aggregate now contain all 37 cases.
    matched37 = {
        variant: {name: core_times[variant][name] if name in core_times[variant]
                  else row['medians_us'][variant]
                  for name, row in all_cases['all_tests'].items()}
        for variant in ('before', 'after')}
    aggregates = {variant: metrics(times, frozen['c37_times_us']) for variant, times in matched37.items()}
    historical = metrics(frozen['historical_go37_times_us'], frozen['c37_times_us'])
    for key, prior_key in [('total', '/'), ('arithmetic', 'μ'), ('median', 'Q₂'), ('geometric', 'G')]:
        if not math.isclose(historical[key], frozen['historical37_aggregates'][prior_key], rel_tol=1e-12):
            raise ValueError('Historical 37-case metrics do not reproduce the official README')
    rows = []
    for name in matched37['after']:
        before, after = matched37['before'][name], matched37['after'][name]
        if name in labels:
            index = labels.index(name)
            samples = {variant: [sample['times_us'][index] for sample in core[variant]['process_runs']]
                       for variant in ['before', 'after']}
        else:
            samples = all_cases['all_tests'][name]['samples_us']
        rows.append({'case': name, 'times_us': {'before': before, 'after': after, 'c': frozen['c37_times_us'][name]},
                     'go_over_c': {variant: times[name] / frozen['c37_times_us'][name] for variant, times in matched37.items()},
                     'samples_us': samples, 'speedup': before / after, 'change_percent': 100 * (after / before - 1),
                     'before_over_historical': before / frozen['historical_go37_times_us'][name]})
    all_regressions = sorted([{'case': name, 'change_percent': case['change_percent'],
                              'medians_us': case['medians_us'], 'samples_us': case['samples_us']}
                             for name, case in all_cases['all_tests'].items() if case['change_percent'] > 5],
                            key=lambda row: -row['change_percent'])
    raw_core = {path.name: path.read_text() for suffix in ['stdout', 'stderr']
                for path in sorted((args.output / 'core').glob('*.' + suffix))}
    report = {'started_at_utc': started, 'completed_at_utc': datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat(),
              'host': platform.platform(), 'machine': platform.machine(), 'host_isolated': False,
              'load_average_start': load_start, 'load_average_end': list(os.getloadavg()),
              'protocol': {'paired_order': 'AB/BA/AB', 'processes_per_build': 3,
                           'primary': '14 App core medians plus 23 AppAll library medians; all four Go/C aggregates use 37 matched cases',
                           'GOGC': '800', 'GOMAXPROCS': 'default', 'pgo': False,
                           'C_reference_remeasured': False, 'JS_reference_remeasured': False,
                           'aggregation': 'median of three process minima for each case'},
              'commands': commands, 'wrapper_sha256': sha(Path(__file__)),
              'frozen_reference': frozen, 'compiler_snapshot': compiler, 'aggregates': aggregates, 'historical_aggregates': historical,
              'primary_times_us': core_times, 'primary_total_ms': {k: sum(v.values())/1000 for k,v in core_times.items()},
              'matched37_times_us': matched37, 'matched37_total_ms': {k: sum(v.values())/1000 for k,v in matched37.items()},
              'core14_aggregates': core_aggregates, 'historical_core14_aggregates': core_historical,
              'c_total_ms': sum(frozen['c37_times_us'].values())/1000,
              'rows_by_go_c_descending': sorted(rows, key=lambda r: -r['go_over_c']['after']),
              'all_case_regressions_over_5_percent': all_regressions,
              'validation': {'processes': 12, 'core_oracles': 84, 'all_oracles': 222,
                             'total_oracles': 306, 'source_and_binary_guards': True},
              'core_manifest': json.loads((args.output / 'core/manifest.json').read_text()),
              'core_campaign': core, 'raw_core_outputs': raw_core, 'all_campaign': all_cases}
    write(args.output / 'results.json', report)
    print(json.dumps({'aggregates': aggregates, 'historical': historical,
                      'totals_ms': report['matched37_total_ms'], 'c_total_ms': report['c_total_ms'],
                      'all_regressions_over_5_percent': all_regressions}, indent=2))


if __name__ == '__main__':
    main()

finally: if temporary is not None and temporary.exists(): temporary.unlink() require(args.readme.read_bytes() == proposed, 'README verification failed after replacement') audit['publication_completed'] = True (output / 'audit.json').write_bytes(json_bytes(audit)) print(json.dumps({'mode': audit['mode'], 'audit_directory': str(output.resolve()), 'changed_cells': structural['changed_cells'], 'eligible_cells': structural['eligible_cells'], 'go_c': summaries['C'], 'go_js': summaries['JS'], 'readme_written': audit['publication_completed']}, ensure_ascii=False, """Run current-wave real record input/alias proofs without collecting timings."""
from pathlib import Path
import argparse,hashlib,json,subprocess
W=Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2];P=W/'proofs'
parser=argparse.ArgumentParser();parser.add_argument('side',choices=['before','after']);args=parser.parse_args()
checks=[]
for script,folder,count in [('record-input-proof.py','runtime-inputs',1134),('record-alias-proof.py','alias-inputs',108),('record-compact-alias-proof.py','compact-alias-inputs',36)]:
 destination=P/(folder+'-'+args.side)
 command=['python3',str(P/script),str(W/(args.side+'-all')),str(destination)]
 result=subprocess.run(command,text=True,capture_output=True)
 (P/(folder+'-'+args.side+'.log')).write_text(result.stdout+result.stderr)
 result.check_returncode()
 path=destination/'manifest.json';m=json.loads(path.read_text())
 assert m['validated'] and m['oracles']==count
 m['artifact_sha256']={p.name:hashlib.sha256(p.read_bytes()).hexdigest() for p in destination.iterdir() if p.is_file() and p.name!='manifest.json'}
 path.write_text(json.dumps(m,indent=2)+'\n')
 if args.side=='after':
  for name in ['inputs.json','expected.txt','stdout.txt']:
   assert (P/(folder+'-before')/name).read_bytes()==(destination/name).read_bytes()

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Read-only independent consistency checks for the archived hot-path campaign."""
import base64, hashlib, json, runpy, sys
from pathlib import Path
sys.dont_write_bytecode = True
WORK = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2]
ROOT = WORK.parents[2]
path = ROOT / 'docs/benchmark-results/2026-11-27-go-traverse-records.json'
raw = path.read_bytes()
archive = json.loads(raw)
sha = lambda data: hashlib.sha256(data).hexdigest()
count = 0


def visit(value):
    global count
    if isinstance(value, dict):
        if isinstance(value.get('text'), str) and 'sha256' in value:
            assert sha(value['text'].encode()) == value['sha256']
            count += 1
        if isinstance(value.get('base64'), str) and 'sha256' in value:
            assert sha(base64.b64decode(value['base64'])) == value['sha256']
        for child in value.values():
            visit(child)
    elif isinstance(value, list):
        for child in value:
            visit(child)


visit(archive)
helper = runpy.run_path(str(Path(__file__).with_name('archive.py')))
checks = helper['check_campaign'](archive['campaign'])
assert checks == archive['validation']['archive_checks']
for name,check in [('runtime_input_proofs',lambda:helper['check_inputs'](archive['campaign'])),('alias_input_proofs',lambda:helper['check_alias_inputs'](archive['campaign'])),('compact_alias_input_proofs',lambda:helper['check_alias_inputs'](archive['campaign'],compact=True))]:
    if archive['validation'][name].get('performed') is not False:
        assert check()==archive['validation'][name]
    else:
        assert archive['validation'][name]['total_oracles']==0
for key, alias in [('array_input_proofs',False),('array_alias_input_proofs',True)]:
    if archive['validation'][key].get('performed') is not False:
        assert helper['check_array_inputs'](archive['campaign'],alias=alias)==archive['validation'][key]
    else:assert archive['validation'][key]['total_oracles']==0
for key,fn in [('sum_input_proofs',lambda:helper['check_sum_inputs'](archive['campaign'])),('sum_wide_input_proofs',lambda:helper['check_sum_inputs'](archive['campaign'],wide=True)),('tree_input_proofs',lambda:helper['check_tree_inputs'](archive['campaign']))]:
    if archive['validation'][key].get('performed') is not False:assert fn()==archive['validation'][key]
    else:assert archive['validation'][key]['total_oracles']==0
assert helper['check_traverse_inputs'](archive['campaign'])==archive['validation']['traverse_input_proofs']
assert helper['check_traverse_inputs'](archive['campaign'],wide=True)==archive['validation']['traverse_wide_input_proofs']
assert helper['check_excluded_campaign'](archive['campaign'])==archive['validation']['excluded_campaigns']
assert helper['check_diagnostics'](archive['campaign']) == archive['validation']['diagnostic_checks']
assert archive['validation']['final_summary'] == json.loads((WORK / 'validation-summary.json').read_text())
assert archive['report']['text'] == (ROOT / archive['report']['path']).read_text()
for name, evidence in archive['validation']['logs'].items():
    assert sha((WORK / name).read_bytes()) == evidence['sha256'], name
for name, evidence in archive['proofs']['runtime_inputs_and_collectors'].items():
    assert sha((WORK / 'proofs' / name).read_bytes()) == evidence['sha256'], name
for name, evidence in archive['proofs']['supporting_files'].items():
    assert sha((WORK / name).read_bytes()) == evidence['sha256'], name
assert not (ROOT / 'bin/benchmark/ratio-measurements.json').exists()
print(json.dumps({'path': str(path), 'bytes': len(raw), 'sha256': sha(raw),
                  'embedded_text_hashes_verified': count, 'campaign': checks,
                  'runtime_oracles': archive['validation']['runtime_input_proofs']['total_oracles'],
                  'alias_oracles': archive['validation']['alias_input_proofs']['total_oracles'],
                  'compact_alias_oracles': archive['validation']['compact_alias_input_proofs']['total_oracles'],
                  'array_oracles': archive['validation']['array_input_proofs']['total_oracles'],
                  'array_alias_oracles': archive['validation']['array_alias_input_proofs']['total_oracles'],
                  'sum_oracles': archive['validation']['sum_input_proofs']['total_oracles'],
                  'sum_wide_oracles': archive['validation']['sum_wide_input_proofs']['total_oracles'],
                  'tree_forest_comparisons': archive['validation']['tree_input_proofs']['total_forest_comparisons'],
                  'traverse_oracles': archive['validation']['traverse_input_proofs']['total_oracles'],
                  'traverse_wide_oracles': archive['validation']['traverse_wide_input_proofs']['total_oracles'],
                  'removed_catalogue_remains_absent': True}, indent=2))

# Generated-code attribution review — traverse + records

Read-only review of every changed Go section, the original benchmark sources and function bodies across package placements. No timing, profile or build was launched for this review. Extracted diffs are in `section-diffs/`; normalized function equality checks are in `generated-worker-comparison.json`, reproducible with `review-record-bodies.py`.

The core output has zero changed sections out of 633. The all output has seven changed sections out of 683, all attributable to the approved transformations and resulting package placement. Package headers, runtime, FFI, entry points and init-order files are byte-identical. Bench timing/batch code and opaque functions are outside the changed set.

## Record workers and package placement

All three native update workers get the same small unsigned-range guard and one field update, returning the native value-copy. Out-of-range counts call a typed cold helper. For small, medium and large, the cold helper is byte-identical to the previous complete worker after replacing only its function name and generated package/runtime aliases. Native parameter/return ABIs are unchanged. No original guard, fallback loop or Int32 narrowing is lost.

All three prepared-action getter bodies are identical after normalizing only package aliases. Record construction, its initial opaque call, capture of the saved opaque action, replay on each timed invocation, per-invocation opaque count 1000, projection guards, generic field fallback, sums and public boxing remain unchanged. The optimized update runs inside each timed action, not just preparation.

Large remains in `p_root`. Medium's public getter, prepared-action getter and fast worker move from `p_root` to the shared package; the original worker remains under its cold name in `p_root`. Small's fast worker and prepared action remain in the shared package, while its cold helper moves to `p_root`. `AppLibrary.go` changes only `gf7c1c4.Get_Test_RecordSetMedium1000_prepare()` to the now-local getter. Labels, registration order and action identity are unchanged. There is no additional benchmark or callback registration.

## Traverse action

Only the success traverse test's returned action body changes. The saved input action is still invoked at the same point on every call. Canonical traversal/applicative dictionary captures retain their original order, followed by the closed mapper and input capture. The intermediate native array, its always-Just wrapper and subsequent pattern match/checksum call become one scalar loop over the original buffer. The mapper still uses IntAdd, and the checksum retains the guarded multiplication, original IntMul fallback and IntAdd ordering. The seed remains 0 and the index retains its existing Int64 conversion.

The changed work executes inside the timed prepared action. Preparation/source fixture generation and opaque barriers remain unchanged. The separate failure-traverse test has no generated diff; no short-circuit rule for unknown or Nothing-producing callbacks is introduced.

## Attribution

Directly changed measured actions: record/set-small-1000, record/set-medium-1000, record/set-large-1000 and traverse/maybe success. Other measured action bodies have no source delta. Package placement can influence machine-code layout, so secondary timing movements are not attributed to a new optimization without separate evidence. This scope review complements the record input/alias proofs, native/source E2E and traverse observations; it does not replace those tests or the paired campaign.

module Gopurs.ModuleWorkers (declaration) where

import Prelude
import Data.Array as Array
import Data.Foldable (any)
import Data.Map as Map
import Data.Maybe (Maybe(..))
import Data.Tuple (Tuple(..), fst, snd)
import Effect.Ref as Ref
import Effect.Unsafe (unsafePerformEffect)
import Gopurs.ExprAnalysis (extractExprFuncType, functionResultAfter, getExprType)
import Gopurs.ExprContext (ExprContext, TranslateExpr, bindParameters, flattenStmts)
import Gopurs.ArrayIndexedFold as ArrayIndexedFold
import Gopurs.CallAnalysis (collectGoSpine, getGoSpineArgs)
import Gopurs.GoAst (GoDecl(..), GoExpr(..), GoType(..))
import Gopurs.GoSymbol (GoReference(..), generated, referenceName)
import Gopurs.GoConversions (boxGoExpr, coerceGoExpr)
import Gopurs.GoFunctions (Parameters, curriedFunction, iterationBindings, loopParameters, namedParameters)
import Gopurs.Int32Loops as Int32Loops
import Gopurs.AffineLoops as AffineLoops
import Gopurs.RecordAffineLoops as RecordAffineLoops
import Gopurs.ArraySnoc as ArraySnoc
import Gopurs.ListFilter as ListFilter
import Gopurs.TailAddLoops as TailAddLoops
import PureScript.Backend.Optimizer.Codegen.Tco (TcoExpr)

type Worker =
  { ident :: String
  , args :: Array String
  , body :: TcoExpr
  , val :: TcoExpr
  }

-- Use precisely the ABI published by ModuleBindings, including native record
-- projections. A self-recursive singleton gets a loop; peers in larger groups
-- remain ordinary calls. Module bodies begin with no captured local bindings.
declaration :: TranslateExpr -> ExprContext -> Boolean -> Worker -> GoDecl
declaration translate context@{ codegenStateRef, modNameStr, moduleFunctions } isSelfRecursive fn =
  let
    info = Map.lookup fn.ident moduleFunctions
    params = namedParameters fn.args (case info of
      Just signature -> signature.fArgs
      Nothing -> [])
    expectedBodyType = map (functionResultAfter (Array.length fn.args)) (extractExprFuncType (getExprType fn.val))
    loop = if isSelfRecursive then
      [ { ident: fn.ident, loopParams: map fst (loopParameters params), goTypes: map snd params } ]
      else []
    workerContext = context
      { depth = 0
      , bound = bindParameters params Map.empty
      , tcoIdent = Just fn.ident
      , loopCtx = loop
      , options = { isTail: isSelfRecursive, inEffectBlock: false }
      , mbExpectedExprType = expectedBodyType
      , mbExpectedGoType = if Array.null fn.args || resultType == TypeValue then Nothing else Just resultType
      }
    resultType = case info of
      Just signature | Array.length fn.args < Array.length signature.fArgs -> TypeValue
      Just signature -> signature.fRet
      Nothing -> TypeValue
    tailAdd = if isSelfRecursive then
      TailAddLoops.worker translate workerContext fn.ident params resultType fn.body
      else Nothing
    body boxed = case tailAdd of
      Just loopBody -> loopBody
      Nothing ->
        let
          native = case ListFilter.worker context.metadata params resultType fn.val of
            Just filtered -> Just filtered
            Nothing -> ArraySnoc.worker modNameStr fn.ident params resultType fn.body
          result = case native of
            Just lowered -> lowered
            Nothing -> translate workerContext 0 fn.body
          returning = if boxed then boxGoExpr codegenStateRef modNameStr result.expr result.exprType
            else coerceGoExpr codegenStateRef modNameStr result.expr result.exprType resultType
          statements = flattenStmts result.stmts <> [ GoReturn returning ]
        in if isSelfRecursive then
          AffineLoops.wrap translate workerContext (AffineLoops.globalTarget modNameStr fn.ident) params resultType fn.body
            (Int32Loops.loop fn.ident params resultType statements)
          else GoBlock (iterationBindings params <> statements)
    value = if Array.null fn.args then
      -- A zero-argument abstraction still defers its whole body until called.
      curriedFunction [ Tuple "_" TypeValue ] TypeValue
        (body true)
      else
        let
          workerName = "Call_" <> modNameStr <> "_" <> fn.ident
          coldIdent = "__gopurs_affine_cold_" <> fn.ident
          coldName = "Call_" <> modNameStr <> "_" <> coldIdent
          reserved = Map.member coldIdent moduleFunctions
            || any (\signature -> referenceName signature.reference == coldName) context.metadata.ffiFunctions
          coldCall = GoCall (GoRef (SymbolReference (generated modNameStr coldName)))
            (map (GoVar <<< fst) (loopParameters params))
          hot = if isSelfRecursive && not reserved then
            RecordAffineLoops.hot (AffineLoops.globalTarget modNameStr fn.ident) params resultType fn.body coldCall
            else Nothing
          original = body false
          declare name workerBody = GoFunctionDecl
            { name: generated modNameStr name, params: loopParameters params, result: resultType, body: workerBody }
          workers = case hot of
            Just fast -> [ declare coldName original, declare workerName fast ]
            Nothing -> [ declare workerName original ]
        in
          unsafePerformEffect do
            Ref.modify_ (\state -> state { declarations = state.declarations <> workers }) codegenStateRef
            pure (case indexedWrapper translate context params fn.body of
              Just wrapper -> wrapper
              Nothing -> boxedWrapper context fn.ident params resultType)
  in
    GoCachedValue { identifier: generated modNameStr (modNameStr <> "_" <> fn.ident), expression: value, goType: TypeValue }

-- A scalar indexed fold can read either representation directly. Keep the
-- public Value wrapper on its original Value buffer instead of first copying
-- it into the native worker's array. Admission is shared with the fold emitter.
indexedWrapper :: TranslateExpr -> ExprContext -> Parameters -> TcoExpr -> Maybe GoExpr
indexedWrapper translate context params body = case params of
  [ Tuple name (TypeNativeArray TypeInt64) ] -> do
    let
      boxedContext = context { bound = bindParameters [ Tuple name TypeValue ] Map.empty }
      Tuple function spine = collectGoSpine body
    result <- ArrayIndexedFold.emit translate boxedContext 0 function (getGoSpineArgs spine)
    pure (GoCall (GoVar "gopurs_runtime.Func")
      [ GoFuncLit [ Tuple name TypeValue ] (flattenStmts result.stmts)
          (boxGoExpr context.codegenStateRef context.modNameStr result.expr result.exprType) TypeValue ])
  _ -> Nothing

-- Module wrappers group up to ten arguments; larger arities keep unary layers.
-- LocalWorkers and anonymous closures retain their own grouping policies.
boxedWrapper :: ExprContext -> String -> Parameters -> GoType -> GoExpr
boxedWrapper { codegenStateRef, modNameStr } name params resultType =
  let
    wrapperParams = map (\(Tuple param _) -> param <> "_box") params
    call = GoCall (GoRef (SymbolReference (generated modNameStr ("Call_" <> modNameStr <> "_" <> name))))
      (map (\(Tuple param ty) -> coerceGoExpr codegenStateRef modNameStr (GoVar (param <> "_box")) TypeValue ty) params)
    boxed = boxGoExpr codegenStateRef modNameStr call resultType
    arity = Array.length params
    wrapperName = if arity == 1 then "gopurs_runtime.Func" else "gopurs_runtime.Func" <> show arity
  in
    if arity <= 10 then
      GoCall (GoVar wrapperName) [ GoFuncLit (map (\param -> Tuple param TypeValue) wrapperParams) [] boxed TypeValue ]
    else Array.foldr
      (\param inner -> GoCall (GoSelector (GoVar "gopurs_runtime") "Func")
        [ GoFuncLit [ Tuple param TypeValue ] [] inner TypeValue ])
      boxed wrapperParams

-- Collapse pure countdown recurrences over immutable native records. The
-- complete update tree is proved before changing the number of iterations.
module Gopurs.RecordAffineLoops (wrap, hot) where

import Prelude

import Control.Alternative (guard)
import Data.Array as Array
import Data.Array.NonEmpty as NEA
import Data.Maybe (Maybe(..))
import Data.Traversable (traverse)
import Data.Tuple (Tuple(..), fst)
import Gopurs.GoAst (GoExpr(..), GoType(..), recordFieldName)
import Gopurs.GoFunctions (Parameters)
import PureScript.Backend.Optimizer.Codegen.Tco (TcoExpr(..))
import PureScript.Backend.Optimizer.CoreFn (Literal(..), Prop(..))
import PureScript.Backend.Optimizer.FreeVars (localId)
import PureScript.Backend.Optimizer.Syntax (BackendSyntax, Pair(..))
import PureScript.Backend.Optimizer.Syntax as Syn

data Delta = Constant Int | Remainders Int
data Change = Keep | Fields GoType (Array (Tuple String Change)) | Add Delta

type Recurrence = { counter :: String, record :: String, changes :: Change }

wrap :: (TcoExpr -> Boolean) -> Parameters -> GoType -> TcoExpr -> GoExpr -> GoExpr
wrap self params result body original = case recognize self params result body of
  Just recurrence ->
    let counter = GoVar (recurrence.counter <> "_loop")
        record = GoVar (recurrence.record <> "_loop")
        admitted = GoBinOp "&&" (GoBinOp ">" counter (integer 0))
          (GoBinOp "<=" counter (integer top))
    in GoBlock [ GoIfElse admitted [ GoReturn (emit counter record recurrence.changes) ] [], original ]
  Nothing -> original

-- A small native wrapper can inline at its callers while the complete old
-- worker remains the cold fallback. Only one flat field and a cheap constant
-- delta are admitted; nested updates and larger expressions keep their layout.
-- The proof of the recurrence is shared with wrap, not reconstructed from Go.
hot :: (TcoExpr -> Boolean) -> Parameters -> GoType -> TcoExpr -> GoExpr -> Maybe GoExpr
hot self params result body fallback = do
  recurrence <- recognize self params result body
  Tuple field delta <- case recurrence.changes of
    Fields _ [ Tuple field (Add (Constant delta)) ] | delta >= (-1) && delta <= 1 -> Just (Tuple field delta)
    _ -> Nothing
  let counter = GoVar (recurrence.counter <> "_loop")
      recordName = recurrence.record <> "_loop"
      record = GoVar recordName
      previous = GoRecordFieldAccess record field
      value = if delta == 0 then previous else GoBinOp (if delta == 1 then "+" else "-") previous counter
      -- For all signed Int64 inputs this unsigned interval is exactly 1..top.
      -- Addition/subtraction modulo 2^64 followed by Int32 narrowing preserves
      -- the original low 32 bits, including noncanonical FFI field values.
      -- Even delta zero must narrow on n>0; n=0 takes the unchanged fallback.
      admitted = GoBinOp "<" (GoBinOp "-" (GoCall (GoVar "uint64") [ counter ]) (GoInt 1)) (GoInt top)
  pure (GoBlock
    [ GoIfElse admitted [ GoMutate (recordName <> "." <> recordFieldName field) (narrow value), GoReturn record ] []
    , GoReturn fallback
    ])

recognize :: (TcoExpr -> Boolean) -> Parameters -> GoType -> TcoExpr -> Maybe Recurrence
recognize self params result body = do
  parameters <- case params of
    [ Tuple counter TypeInt64, Tuple record ty@(TypeRecord _) ] ->
      Just { counter, record, ty, counterFirst: true }
    [ Tuple record ty@(TypeRecord _), Tuple counter TypeInt64 ] ->
      Just { counter, record, ty, counterFirst: false }
    _ -> Nothing
  guard (parameters.counter /= parameters.record && result == parameters.ty)
  branch <- case syntax body of
    Syn.Branch branches step -> case NEA.toArray branches of
      [ Pair condition seed ] -> Just { condition, seed, step }
      _ -> Nothing
    _ -> Nothing
  guard (case syntax branch.condition of
    Syn.PrimOp (Syn.Op2 (Syn.OpIntOrd Syn.OpEq) left right) ->
      (local parameters.counter left && literal 0 right)
        || (literal 0 left && local parameters.counter right)
    _ -> false)
  guard (local parameters.record branch.seed)
  arguments <- case syntax branch.step of
    Syn.App target args | self target -> Just (NEA.toArray args)
    Syn.UncurriedApp target args | self target -> Just args
    _ -> Nothing
  Tuple nextCounter nextRecord <- case arguments of
    [ first, second ] -> Just (if parameters.counterFirst then Tuple first second else Tuple second first)
    _ -> Nothing
  guard (case syntax nextCounter of
    Syn.PrimOp (Syn.Op2 (Syn.OpIntNum Syn.OpSubtract) left right) ->
      local parameters.counter left && literal 1 right
    _ -> false)
  changes <- recordChanges parameters.counter parameters.record [] parameters.ty nextRecord
  pure { counter: parameters.counter, record: parameters.record, changes }

-- Every updated leaf reads its own previous value. Cross-field dependencies,
-- calls, effects, duplicate updates and layout changes retain the original loop.
-- Unchanged fields are copied by value, including any borrowed references.
recordChanges :: String -> String -> Array String -> GoType -> TcoExpr -> Maybe Change
recordChanges counter record path ty expression
  | recordPath record expression == Just path = Just Keep
  | otherwise = case ty, syntax expression of
      recordType@(TypeRecord fields), Syn.Update source props -> do
        guard (recordPath record source == Just path)
        let keys = map (\(Prop key _) -> key) props
        guard (Array.length (Array.nub keys) == Array.length keys)
        guard (Array.length (Array.nub (map fst fields)) == Array.length fields)
        updates <- traverse (\(Prop key value) -> do
          Tuple _ fieldType <- Array.find (\(Tuple label _) -> label == key) fields
          change <- recordChanges counter record (Array.snoc path key) fieldType value
          pure (Tuple key change)) props
        pure (Fields recordType updates)
      TypeInt64, Syn.PrimOp (Syn.Op2 (Syn.OpIntNum Syn.OpAdd) left right)
        | recordPath record left == Just path -> Add <$> increment counter right
        | recordPath record right == Just path -> Add <$> increment counter left
      _, _ -> Nothing

increment :: String -> TcoExpr -> Maybe Delta
increment counter expression = case syntax expression of
  Syn.Lit (LitInt value) | value >= bottom && value <= top -> Just (Constant value)
  Syn.PrimOp (Syn.Op2 (Syn.OpIntNum Syn.OpMod) value divisor) | local counter value -> do
    modulus <- intLiteral divisor
    guard (modulus > 0 && modulus <= top)
    pure (Remainders modulus)
  _ -> Nothing

emit :: GoExpr -> GoExpr -> Change -> GoExpr
emit counter original = case _ of
  Keep -> original
  Fields ty fields -> GoRecordUpdateNative ty original
    (map (\(Tuple key change) -> Tuple key (emit counter (GoRecordFieldAccess original key) change)) fields)
  Add delta ->
    -- At least one IntAdd executes on the admitted path. Normalize its seed
    -- first, so even noncanonical Int64 FFI inputs need no overflow assumption.
    -- n and each literal fit Int32; products and their sum fit signed Int64.
    narrow (GoBinOp "+" (narrow original) (total counter delta))

total :: GoExpr -> Delta -> GoExpr
total count = case _ of
  Constant value -> GoBinOp "*" count (integer value)
  Remainders modulus ->
    let divisor = integer modulus
        quotient = GoBinOp "/" count divisor
        remainder = GoBinOp "%" count divisor
        cycles = GoBinOp "/" (GoBinOp "*" (GoBinOp "*" quotient divisor) (integer (modulus - 1))) (integer 2)
        suffix = GoBinOp "/" (GoBinOp "*" remainder (GoBinOp "+" remainder (integer 1))) (integer 2)
    -- Sum k mod d for k=1..n: complete periods plus the final 1..remainder.
    in GoBinOp "+" cycles suffix

syntax :: TcoExpr -> BackendSyntax TcoExpr
syntax (TcoExpr _ value) = case value of
  Syn.Typed _ inner -> syntax inner
  Syn.TypeApp inner _ -> syntax inner
  _ -> value

local :: String -> TcoExpr -> Boolean
local name expression = case syntax expression of
  Syn.Local ident level -> localId ident level == name
  _ -> false

recordPath :: String -> TcoExpr -> Maybe (Array String)
recordPath root expression = case syntax expression of
  Syn.Local ident level | localId ident level == root -> Just []
  Syn.Accessor source (Syn.GetProp key) -> map (flip Array.snoc key) (recordPath root source)
  _ -> Nothing

intLiteral :: TcoExpr -> Maybe Int
intLiteral expression = case syntax expression of
  Syn.Lit (LitInt value) -> Just value
  _ -> Nothing

literal :: Int -> TcoExpr -> Boolean
literal value expression = intLiteral expression == Just value

narrow :: GoExpr -> GoExpr
narrow value = GoCall (GoVar "int64") [ GoCall (GoVar "int32") [ value ] ]

integer :: Int -> GoExpr
integer value = GoCall (GoVar "int64") [ GoInt value ]

module Main where

import Prelude
import Data.Foldable (for_)
import Effect (Effect)
import Effect.Console (logShow)
import Effect.Ref as Ref
import Subject as Subject

main :: Effect Unit
main = do
  source <- Ref.new { total: 2147483647, borrowed: [ 7, 11 ], stamp: "retained" }
  counts <- Ref.new [ 0, 1, 2, 7, 1000 ]
  values <- Ref.read counts
  for_ values \count -> do
    input <- Ref.read source
    logShow [ (Subject.step count input).total, (Subject.normalize count input).total, (Subject.down count input).total ]
  input <- Ref.read source
  logShow input.total
  logShow input.borrowed
  logShow input.stamp

module Subject where

import Prelude

type Snapshot = { total :: Int, borrowed :: Array Int, stamp :: String }

step :: Int -> Snapshot -> Snapshot
step 0 snapshot = snapshot
step remaining snapshot = step (remaining - 1) (snapshot { total = snapshot.total + 1 })

normalize :: Int -> Snapshot -> Snapshot
normalize 0 snapshot = snapshot
normalize remaining snapshot = normalize (remaining - 1) (snapshot { total = snapshot.total + 0 })

down :: Int -> Snapshot -> Snapshot
down 0 snapshot = snapshot
down remaining snapshot = down (remaining - 1) (snapshot { total = snapshot.total + (-1) })

-- Collapse pure countdown recurrences over immutable native records. The
-- complete update tree is proved before changing the number of iterations.
module Gopurs.RecordAffineLoops (wrap) where

import Prelude

import Control.Alternative (guard)
import Data.Array as Array
import Data.Array.NonEmpty as NEA
import Data.Maybe (Maybe(..))
import Data.Traversable (traverse)
import Data.Tuple (Tuple(..), fst)
import Gopurs.GoAst (GoExpr(..), GoType(..))
import Gopurs.GoFunctions (Parameters)
import PureScript.Backend.Optimizer.Codegen.Tco (TcoExpr(..))
import PureScript.Backend.Optimizer.CoreFn (Literal(..), Prop(..))
import PureScript.Backend.Optimizer.FreeVars (localId)
import PureScript.Backend.Optimizer.Syntax (BackendSyntax, Pair(..))
import PureScript.Backend.Optimizer.Syntax as Syn

data Delta = Constant Int | Remainders Int
data Change = Keep | Fields GoType (Array (Tuple String Change)) | Add Delta

type Recurrence = { counter :: String, record :: String, changes :: Change }

wrap :: (TcoExpr -> Boolean) -> Parameters -> GoType -> TcoExpr -> GoExpr -> GoExpr
wrap self params result body original = case recognize self params result body of
  Just recurrence ->
    let counter = GoVar (recurrence.counter <> "_loop")
        record = GoVar (recurrence.record <> "_loop")
        admitted = GoBinOp "&&" (GoBinOp ">" counter (integer 0))
          (GoBinOp "<=" counter (integer top))
    in GoBlock [ GoIfElse admitted [ GoReturn (emit counter record recurrence.changes) ] [], original ]
  Nothing -> original

recognize :: (TcoExpr -> Boolean) -> Parameters -> GoType -> TcoExpr -> Maybe Recurrence
recognize self params result body = do
  parameters <- case params of
    [ Tuple counter TypeInt64, Tuple record ty@(TypeRecord _) ] ->
      Just { counter, record, ty, counterFirst: true }
    [ Tuple record ty@(TypeRecord _), Tuple counter TypeInt64 ] ->
      Just { counter, record, ty, counterFirst: false }
    _ -> Nothing
  guard (parameters.counter /= parameters.record && result == parameters.ty)
  branch <- case syntax body of
    Syn.Branch branches step -> case NEA.toArray branches of
      [ Pair condition seed ] -> Just { condition, seed, step }
      _ -> Nothing
    _ -> Nothing
  guard (case syntax branch.condition of
    Syn.PrimOp (Syn.Op2 (Syn.OpIntOrd Syn.OpEq) left right) ->
      (local parameters.counter left && literal 0 right)
        || (literal 0 left && local parameters.counter right)
    _ -> false)
  guard (local parameters.record branch.seed)
  arguments <- case syntax branch.step of
    Syn.App target args | self target -> Just (NEA.toArray args)
    Syn.UncurriedApp target args | self target -> Just args
    _ -> Nothing
  Tuple nextCounter nextRecord <- case arguments of
    [ first, second ] -> Just (if parameters.counterFirst then Tuple first second else Tuple second first)
    _ -> Nothing
  guard (case syntax nextCounter of
    Syn.PrimOp (Syn.Op2 (Syn.OpIntNum Syn.OpSubtract) left right) ->
      local parameters.counter left && literal 1 right
    _ -> false)
  changes <- recordChanges parameters.counter parameters.record [] parameters.ty nextRecord
  pure { counter: parameters.counter, record: parameters.record, changes }

-- Every updated leaf reads its own previous value. Cross-field dependencies,
-- calls, effects, duplicate updates and layout changes retain the original loop.
-- Unchanged fields are copied by value, including any borrowed references.
recordChanges :: String -> String -> Array String -> GoType -> TcoExpr -> Maybe Change
recordChanges counter record path ty expression
  | recordPath record expression == Just path = Just Keep
  | otherwise = case ty, syntax expression of
      recordType@(TypeRecord fields), Syn.Update source props -> do
        guard (recordPath record source == Just path)
        let keys = map (\(Prop key _) -> key) props
        guard (Array.length (Array.nub keys) == Array.length keys)
        guard (Array.length (Array.nub (map fst fields)) == Array.length fields)
        updates <- traverse (\(Prop key value) -> do
          Tuple _ fieldType <- Array.find (\(Tuple label _) -> label == key) fields
          change <- recordChanges counter record (Array.snoc path key) fieldType value
          pure (Tuple key change)) props
        pure (Fields recordType updates)
      TypeInt64, Syn.PrimOp (Syn.Op2 (Syn.OpIntNum Syn.OpAdd) left right)
        | recordPath record left == Just path -> Add <$> increment counter right
        | recordPath record right == Just path -> Add <$> increment counter left
      _, _ -> Nothing

increment :: String -> TcoExpr -> Maybe Delta
increment counter expression = case syntax expression of
  Syn.Lit (LitInt value) | value >= bottom && value <= top -> Just (Constant value)
  Syn.PrimOp (Syn.Op2 (Syn.OpIntNum Syn.OpMod) value divisor) | local counter value -> do
    modulus <- intLiteral divisor
    guard (modulus > 0 && modulus <= top)
    pure (Remainders modulus)
  _ -> Nothing

emit :: GoExpr -> GoExpr -> Change -> GoExpr
emit counter original = case _ of
  Keep -> original
  Fields ty fields -> GoRecordUpdateNative ty original
    (map (\(Tuple key change) -> Tuple key (emit counter (GoRecordFieldAccess original key) change)) fields)
  Add delta ->
    -- At least one IntAdd executes on the admitted path. Normalize its seed
    -- first, so even noncanonical Int64 FFI inputs need no overflow assumption.
    -- n and each literal fit Int32; products and their sum fit signed Int64.
    narrow (GoBinOp "+" (narrow original) (total counter delta))

total :: GoExpr -> Delta -> GoExpr
total count = case _ of
  Constant value -> GoBinOp "*" count (integer value)
  Remainders modulus ->
    let divisor = integer modulus
        quotient = GoBinOp "/" count divisor
        remainder = GoBinOp "%" count divisor
        cycles = GoBinOp "/" (GoBinOp "*" (GoBinOp "*" quotient divisor) (integer (modulus - 1))) (integer 2)
        suffix = GoBinOp "/" (GoBinOp "*" remainder (GoBinOp "+" remainder (integer 1))) (integer 2)
    -- Sum k mod d for k=1..n: complete periods plus the final 1..remainder.
    in GoBinOp "+" cycles suffix

syntax :: TcoExpr -> BackendSyntax TcoExpr
syntax (TcoExpr _ value) = case value of
  Syn.Typed _ inner -> syntax inner
  Syn.TypeApp inner _ -> syntax inner
  _ -> value

local :: String -> TcoExpr -> Boolean
local name expression = case syntax expression of
  Syn.Local ident level -> localId ident level == name
  _ -> false

recordPath :: String -> TcoExpr -> Maybe (Array String)
recordPath root expression = case syntax expression of
  Syn.Local ident level | localId ident level == root -> Just []
  Syn.Accessor source (Syn.GetProp key) -> map (flip Array.snoc key) (recordPath root source)
  _ -> Nothing

intLiteral :: TcoExpr -> Maybe Int
intLiteral expression = case syntax expression of
  Syn.Lit (LitInt value) -> Just value
  _ -> Nothing

literal :: Int -> TcoExpr -> Boolean
literal value expression = intLiteral expression == Just value

narrow :: GoExpr -> GoExpr
narrow value = GoCall (GoVar "int64") [ GoCall (GoVar "int32") [ value ] ]

integer :: Int -> GoExpr
integer value = GoCall (GoVar "int64") [ GoInt value ]

# 🌈 PureScript universal multi-runtime benchmark ## Project goal This project is a **proof of concept** demonstrating the power of abstraction and portability offered by **PureScript**. The goal is to show how the exact same pure functional code (without any manual FFI) can be compiled and executed natively on radically different ecosystems. Backends consume either standard `CoreFn` or, for the local AOT backends, the typed `TAST/tcorefn` representation exported by a local PureScript fork (may be subject to an official PR soon). ## Comprehensive benchmarks The benchmark suite runs a **wide variety** of computationally intensive tasks: AST evaluation, massive list processing, tail call optimization, deep record updates... These tests apply massive **pressure** on the call stack, garbage collector, disk I/O, event loops, and runtime execution engines to measure the raw ability of the compiler and the underlying virtual machine. > [!NOTE] > **Reading the benchmark tables** > > - **Status, only for gopurs, purust, phpurs, sharpurs and javapurs:** **Stable** = measured and considered fully optimized; **WIP** = measured, with optimization work remaining; **Backlog** = planned work without a published measurement or ratio. Status labels belong only to the relevant backend columns. References and external backends have no status. Stable is currently empty, including for Go: the available analyses still identify optimization opportunities. > - **Ratios:** `/C` uses the optimized imperative C reference; `/JS` uses the first JavaScript column. **Below 1× is faster; above 1× is slower.** Extended Results uses its own JS reference and has no C reference. > - **Totals:** sums of the available per-test medians: **Total WIP** for the controlled backends, **Total** for references and external backends. Backlog never contributes. Empty Stable groups are shown as *Coming soon...* and have no defined total, ratio or mean. These totals do not represent an application benchmark. > - **Summaries:** `μ` = arithmetic mean, `Q₂` = median, `G` = geometric mean of the case ratios. Each case has equal weight. All four ratios use exactly the same measured cases on both sides: Go/C and Go/JS both cover all 37 measured Go cases. The full total of a reference table is not used as a denominator for a different set of cases. Very small reference times can produce large ratios. > - **Missing data:** `—` means unavailable or not applicable, never zero. Bounds (`< …`) are excluded from summaries. `n=a/b` indicates coverage: measured cases out of listed cases for a time total, or matched references out of measured cases for a ratio. Historical diagnostic measurements remain in the reference tables; their controlled-backend counterparts belong to unmeasured Backlog. > - **Display precision, in every table:** values ≥ 1 use two decimal places (`12.000045 → 12.00`); positive values < 1 keep two significant digits after leading zeros (`0.000045`, `0.009492 → 0.0095`). Zero is `0.00`. > - **Opaque inputs, in every table:** inputs must remain unknown to the optimizer at runtime. Algebraic simplification is allowed; substituting the driver’s known input is not. > - **Calculations:** use archived timings before display rounding, including for threshold checks. `≈` marks a fallback to published precision. ### Core stresstest benchmark results (pure computational) **Core tests (`src/`)** cover features common to all tested targets (`./bin/run`) #### JavaScript JS Benchmark | Hand-written PureScript

# 🌈 PureScript universal multi-runtime benchmark ## Project goal This project is a **proof of concept** demonstrating the power of abstraction and portability offered by **PureScript**. The goal is to show how the exact same pure functional code (without any manual FFI) can be compiled and executed natively on radically different ecosystems. Backends consume either standard `CoreFn` or, for the local AOT backends, the typed `TAST/tcorefn` representation exported by a local PureScript fork (may be subject to an official PR soon). ## Comprehensive benchmarks The benchmark suite runs a **wide variety** of computationally intensive tasks: AST evaluation, massive list processing, tail call optimization, deep record updates... These tests apply massive **pressure** on the call stack, garbage collector, disk I/O, event loops, and runtime execution engines to measure the raw ability of the compiler and the underlying virtual machine. > [!NOTE] > **Reading the benchmark tables** > > - **Status, only for gopurs, purust, phpurs, sharpurs and javapurs:** **Stable** = measured and considered fully optimized; **WIP** = measured, with optimization work remaining; **Backlog** = planned work without a published measurement or ratio. Status labels belong only to the relevant backend columns. References and external backends have no status. Stable is currently empty, including for Go: the available analyses still identify optimization opportunities. > - **Ratios:** `/C` uses the optimized imperative C reference; `/JS` uses the first JavaScript column. **Below 1× is faster; above 1× is slower.** Extended Results uses its own JS reference and has no C reference. > - **Totals:** sums of the available per-test medians: **Total WIP** for the controlled backends, **Total** for references and external backends. Backlog never contributes. Empty Stable groups are shown as *Coming soon...* and have no defined total, ratio or mean. These totals do not represent an application benchmark. > - **Summaries:** `μ` = arithmetic mean, `Q₂` = median, `G` = geometric mean of the case ratios. Each case has equal weight. All four ratios use exactly the same measured cases on both sides: Go/C and Go/JS both cover all 37 measured Go cases. The full total of a reference table is not used as a denominator for a different set of cases. Very small reference times can produce large ratios. > - **Missing data:** `—` means unavailable or not applicable, never zero. Bounds (`< …`) are excluded from summaries. `n=a/b` indicates coverage: measured cases out of listed cases for a time total, or matched references out of measured cases for a ratio. Historical diagnostic measurements remain in the reference tables; their controlled-backend counterparts belong to unmeasured Backlog. > - **Display precision, in every table:** values ≥ 1 use two decimal places (`12.000045 → 12.00`); positive values < 1 keep two significant digits after leading zeros (`0.000045`, `0.009492 → 0.0095`). Zero is `0.00`. > - **Opaque inputs, in every table:** inputs must remain unknown to the optimizer at runtime. Algebraic simplification is allowed; substituting the driver’s known input is not. > - **Calculations:** use archived timings before display rounding, including for threshold checks. `≈` marks a fallback to published precision. ### Core stresstest benchmark results (pure computational) **Core tests (`src/`)** cover features common to all tested targets (`./bin/run`) #### JavaScript JS Benchmark | Hand-written PureScript

# 🌈 PureScript universal multi-runtime benchmark ## Project goal This project is a **proof of concept** demonstrating the power of abstraction and portability offered by **PureScript**. The goal is to show how the exact same pure functional code (without any manual FFI) can be compiled and executed natively on radically different ecosystems. Backends consume either standard `CoreFn` or, for the local AOT backends, the typed `TAST/tcorefn` representation exported by a local PureScript fork (may be subject to an official PR soon). ## Comprehensive benchmarks The benchmark suite runs a **wide variety** of computationally intensive tasks: AST evaluation, massive list processing, tail call optimization, deep record updates... These tests apply massive **pressure** on the call stack, garbage collector, disk I/O, event loops, and runtime execution engines to measure the raw ability of the compiler and the underlying virtual machine. > [!NOTE] > **Reading the benchmark tables** > > - **Status, only for gopurs, purust, phpurs, sharpurs and javapurs:** **Stable** = measured and considered fully optimized; **WIP** = measured, with optimization work remaining; **Backlog** = planned work without a published measurement or ratio. Status labels belong only to the relevant backend columns. References and external backends have no status. Stable is currently empty, including for Go: the available analyses still identify optimization opportunities. > - **Ratios:** `/C` uses the optimized imperative C reference; `/JS` uses the first JavaScript column. **Below 1× is faster; above 1× is slower.** Extended Results uses its own JS reference and has no C reference. > - **Totals:** sums of the available per-test medians: **Total WIP** for the controlled backends, **Total** for references and external backends. Backlog never contributes. Empty Stable groups are shown as *Coming soon...* and have no defined total, ratio or mean. These totals do not represent an application benchmark. > - **Summaries:** `μ` = arithmetic mean, `Q₂` = median, `G` = geometric mean of the case ratios. Each case has equal weight. All four ratios use exactly the same measured cases on both sides: Go/C and Go/JS both cover all 37 measured Go cases. The full total of a reference table is not used as a denominator for a different set of cases. Very small reference times can produce large ratios. > - **Missing data:** `—` means unavailable or not applicable, never zero. Bounds (`< …`) are excluded from summaries. `n=a/b` indicates coverage: measured cases out of listed cases for a time total, or matched references out of measured cases for a ratio. Historical diagnostic measurements remain in the reference tables; their controlled-backend counterparts belong to unmeasured Backlog. > - **Display precision, in every table:** values ≥ 1 use two decimal places (`12.000045 → 12.00`); positive values < 1 keep two significant digits after leading zeros (`0.000045`, `0.009492 → 0.0095`). Zero is `0.00`. > - **Opaque inputs, in every table:** inputs must remain unknown to the optimizer at runtime. Algebraic simplification is allowed; substituting the driver’s known input is not. > - **Calculations:** use archived timings before display rounding, including for threshold checks. `≈` marks a fallback to published precision. ### Core stresstest benchmark results (pure computational) **Core tests (`src/`)** cover features common to all tested targets (`./bin/run`) #### JavaScript JS Benchmark | Hand-written PureScript

# 🌈 PureScript universal multi-runtime benchmark ## Project goal This project is a **proof of concept** demonstrating the power of abstraction and portability offered by **PureScript**. The goal is to show how the exact same pure functional code (without any manual FFI) can be compiled and executed natively on radically different ecosystems. Backends consume either standard `CoreFn` or, for the local AOT backends, the typed `TAST/tcorefn` representation exported by a local PureScript fork (may be subject to an official PR soon). ## Comprehensive benchmarks The benchmark suite runs a **wide variety** of computationally intensive tasks: AST evaluation, massive list processing, tail call optimization, deep record updates... These tests apply massive **pressure** on the call stack, garbage collector, disk I/O, event loops, and runtime execution engines to measure the raw ability of the compiler and the underlying virtual machine. > [!NOTE] > **Reading the benchmark tables** > > - **Status, only for gopurs, purust, phpurs, sharpurs and javapurs:** **Stable** = measured and considered fully optimized; **WIP** = measured, with optimization work remaining; **Backlog** = planned work without a published measurement or ratio. Status labels belong only to the relevant backend columns. References and external backends have no status. Stable is currently empty, including for Go: the available analyses still identify optimization opportunities. > - **Ratios:** `/C` uses the optimized imperative C reference; `/JS` uses the first JavaScript column. **Below 1× is faster; above 1× is slower.** Extended Results uses its own JS reference and has no C reference. > - **Totals:** sums of the available per-test medians: **Total WIP** for the controlled backends, **Total** for references and external backends. Backlog never contributes. Empty Stable groups are shown as *Coming soon...* and have no defined total, ratio or mean. These totals do not represent an application benchmark. > - **Summaries:** `μ` = arithmetic mean, `Q₂` = median, `G` = geometric mean of the case ratios. Each case has equal weight. All four ratios use exactly the same measured cases on both sides: Go/C and Go/JS both cover all 37 measured Go cases. The full total of a reference table is not used as a denominator for a different set of cases. Very small reference times can produce large ratios. > - **Missing data:** `—` means unavailable or not applicable, never zero. Bounds (`< …`) are excluded from summaries. `n=a/b` indicates coverage: measured cases out of listed cases for a time total, or matched references out of measured cases for a ratio. Historical diagnostic measurements remain in the reference tables; their controlled-backend counterparts belong to unmeasured Backlog. > - **Display precision, in every table:** values ≥ 1 use two decimal places (`12.000045 → 12.00`); positive values < 1 keep two significant digits after leading zeros (`0.000045`, `0.009492 → 0.0095`). Zero is `0.00`. > - **Opaque inputs, in every table:** inputs must remain unknown to the optimizer at runtime. # 🌈 PureScript universal multi-runtime benchmark ## Project goal This project is a **proof of concept** demonstrating the power of abstraction and portability offered by **PureScript**. The goal is to show how the exact same pure functional code (without any manual FFI) can be compiled and executed natively on radically different ecosystems. Backends consume either standard `CoreFn` or, for the local AOT backends, the typed `TAST/tcorefn` representation exported by a local PureScript fork (may be subject to an official PR soon). ## Comprehensive benchmarks The benchmark suite runs a **wide variety** of computationally intensive tasks: AST evaluation, massive list processing, tail call optimization, deep record updates... These tests apply massive **pressure** on the call stack, garbage collector, disk I/O, event loops, and runtime execution engines to measure the raw ability of the compiler and the underlying virtual machine. > [!NOTE] > **Reading the benchmark tables** > > - **Status, only for gopurs, purust, phpurs, sharpurs and javapurs:** **Stable** = measured and considered fully optimized; **WIP** = measured, with optimization work remaining; **Backlog** = planned work without a published measurement or ratio. Status labels belong only to the relevant backend columns. References and external backends have no status. Stable is currently empty, including for Go: the available analyses still identify optimization opportunities. > - **Ratios:** `/C` uses the optimized imperative C reference; `/JS` uses the first JavaScript column. **Below 1× is faster; above 1× is slower.** Extended Results uses its own JS reference and has no C reference. > - **Totals:** sums of the available per-test medians: **Total WIP** for the controlled backends, **Total** for references and external backends. Backlog never contributes. Empty Stable groups are shown as *Coming soon...* and have no defined total, ratio or mean. These totals do not represent an application benchmark. > - **Summaries:** `μ` = arithmetic mean, `Q₂` = median, `G` = geometric mean of the case ratios. Each case has equal weight. All four ratios use exactly the same measured cases on both sides: Go/C and Go/JS both cover all 37 measured Go cases. The full total of a reference table is not used as a denominator for a different set of cases. Very small reference times can produce large ratios. > - **Missing data:** `—` means unavailable or not applicable, never zero. Bounds (`< …`) are excluded from summaries. `n=a/b` indicates coverage: measured cases out of listed cases for a time total, or matched references out of measured cases for a ratio. Historical diagnostic measurements remain in the reference tables; their controlled-backend counterparts belong to unmeasured Backlog. > - **Display precision, in every table:** values ≥ 1 use two decimal places (`12.000045 → 12.00`); positive values < 1 keep two significant digits after leading zeros (`0.000045`, `0.009492 → 0.0095`). Zero is `0.00`. > - **Opaque inputs, in every table:** inputs must remain unknown to the optimizer at runtime. Algebraic simplification is allowed; substituting the driver’s known input is not. > - **Calculations:** use archived timings before display rounding, including for threshold checks. `≈` marks a fallback to published precision. ### Core stresstest benchmark results (pure computational) **Core tests (`src/`)** cover features common to all tested targets (`./bin/run`) #### JavaScript JS Benchmark | Hand-written PureScript

# 🌈 PureScript universal multi-runtime benchmark ## Project goal This project is a **proof of concept** demonstrating the power of abstraction and portability offered by **PureScript**. The goal is to show how the exact same pure functional code (without any manual FFI) can be compiled and executed natively on radically different ecosystems. Backends consume either standard `CoreFn` or, for the local AOT backends, the typed `TAST/tcorefn` representation exported by a local PureScript fork (may be subject to an official PR soon). ## Comprehensive benchmarks The benchmark suite runs a **wide variety** of computationally intensive tasks: AST evaluation, massive list processing, tail call optimization, deep record updates... These tests apply massive **pressure** on the call stack, garbage collector, disk I/O, event loops, and runtime execution engines to measure the raw ability of the compiler and the underlying virtual machine. > [!NOTE] > **Reading the benchmark tables** > > - **Status, only for gopurs, purust, phpurs, sharpurs and javapurs:** **Stable** = measured and considered fully optimized; **WIP** = measured, with optimization work remaining; **Backlog** = planned work without a published measurement or ratio. Status labels belong only to the relevant backend columns. References and external backends have no status. Stable is currently empty, including for Go: the available analyses still identify optimization opportunities. > - **Ratios:** `/C` uses the optimized imperative C reference; `/JS` uses the first JavaScript column. **Below 1× is faster; above 1× is slower.** Extended Results uses its own JS reference and has no C reference. > - **Totals:** sums of the available per-test medians: **Total WIP** for the controlled backends, **Total** for references and external backends. Backlog never contributes. Empty Stable groups are shown as *Coming soon...* and have no defined total, ratio or mean. These totals do not represent an application benchmark. > - **Summaries:** `μ` = arithmetic mean, `Q₂` = median, `G` = geometric mean of the case ratios. Each case has equal weight. All four ratios use exactly the same measured cases on both sides: Go/C and Go/JS both cover all 37 measured Go cases. The full total of a reference table is not used as a denominator for a different set of cases. Very small reference times can produce large ratios. > - **Missing data:** `—` means unavailable or not applicable, never zero. Bounds (`< …`) are excluded from summaries. `n=a/b` indicates coverage: measured cases out of listed cases for a time total, or matched references out of measured cases for a ratio. Historical diagnostic measurements remain in the reference tables; their controlled-backend counterparts belong to unmeasured Backlog. > - **Display precision, in every table:** values ≥ 1 use two decimal places (`12.000045 → 12.00`); positive values < 1 keep two significant digits after leading zeros (`0.000045`, `0.009492 → 0.0095`). Zero is `0.00`. > - **Opaque inputs, in every table:** inputs must remain unknown to the optimizer at runtime. Algebraic simplification is allowed; substituting the driver’s known input is not. > - **Calculations:** use archived timings before display rounding, including for threshold checks. `≈` marks a fallback to published precision. ### Core stresstest benchmark results (pure computational) **Core tests (`src/`)** cover features common to all tested targets (`./bin/run`) #### JavaScript JS Benchmark | Hand-written PureScript

# 🌈 PureScript universal multi-runtime benchmark ## Project goal This project is a **proof of concept** demonstrating the power of abstraction and portability offered by **PureScript**. The goal is to show how the exact same pure functional code (without any manual FFI) can be compiled and executed natively on radically different ecosystems. Backends consume either standard `CoreFn` or, for the local AOT backends, the typed `TAST/tcorefn` representation exported by a local PureScript fork (may be subject to an official PR soon). ## Comprehensive benchmarks The benchmark suite runs a **wide variety** of computationally intensive tasks: AST evaluation, massive list processing, tail call optimization, deep record updates... These tests apply massive **pressure** on the call stack, garbage collector, disk I/O, event loops, and runtime execution engines to measure the raw ability of the compiler and the underlying virtual machine. > [!NOTE] > **Reading the benchmark tables** > > - **Status, only for gopurs, purust, phpurs, sharpurs and javapurs:** **Stable** = measured and considered fully optimized; **WIP** = measured, with optimization work remaining; **Backlog** = planned work without a published measurement or ratio. Status labels belong only to the relevant backend columns. References and external backends have no status. Stable is currently empty, including for Go: the available analyses still identify optimization opportunities. > - **Ratios:** `/C` uses the optimized imperative C reference; `/JS` uses the first JavaScript column. **Below 1× is faster; above 1× is slower.** Extended Results uses its own JS reference and has no C reference. > - **Totals:** sums of the available per-test medians: **Total WIP** for the controlled backends, **Total** for references and external backends. Backlog never contributes. Empty Stable groups are shown as *Coming soon...* and have no defined total, ratio or mean. These totals do not represent an application benchmark. > - **Summaries:** `μ` = arithmetic mean, `Q₂` = median, `G` = geometric mean of the case ratios. Each case has equal weight. All four ratios use exactly the same measured cases on both sides: Go/C and Go/JS both cover all 37 measured Go cases. The full total of a reference table is not used as a denominator for a different set of cases. Very small reference times can produce large ratios. > - **Missing data:** `—` means unavailable or not applicable, never zero. Bounds (`< …`) are excluded from summaries. `n=a/b` indicates coverage: measured cases out of listed cases for a time total, or matched references out of measured cases for a ratio. Historical diagnostic measurements remain in the reference tables; their controlled-backend counterparts belong to unmeasured Backlog. > - **Display precision, in every table:** values ≥ 1 use two decimal places (`12.000045 → 12.00`); positive values < 1 keep two significant digits after leading zeros (`0.000045`, `0.009492 → 0.0095`). Zero is `0.00`. > - **Opaque inputs, in every table:** inputs must remain unknown to the optimizer at runtime. # 🌈 PureScript universal multi-runtime benchmark ## Project goal This project is a **proof of concept** demonstrating the power of abstraction and portability offered by **PureScript**. The goal is to show how the exact same pure functional code (without any manual FFI) can be compiled and executed natively on radically different ecosystems. Backends consume either standard `CoreFn` or, for the local AOT backends, the typed `TAST/tcorefn` representation exported by a local PureScript fork (may be subject to an official PR soon). ## Comprehensive benchmarks The benchmark suite runs a **wide variety** of computationally intensive tasks: AST evaluation, massive list processing, tail call optimization, deep record updates... These tests apply massive **pressure** on the call stack, garbage collector, disk I/O, event loops, and runtime execution engines to measure the raw ability of the compiler and the underlying virtual machine. > [!NOTE] > **Reading the benchmark tables** > > - **Status, only for gopurs, purust, phpurs, sharpurs and javapurs:** **Stable** = measured and considered fully optimized; **WIP** = measured, with optimization work remaining; **Backlog** = planned work without a published measurement or ratio. Status labels belong only to the relevant backend columns. References and external backends have no status. Stable is currently empty, including for Go: the available analyses still identify optimization opportunities. > - **Ratios:** `/C` uses the optimized imperative C reference; `/JS` uses the first JavaScript column. **Below 1× is faster; above 1× is slower.** Extended Results uses its own JS reference and has no C reference. > - **Totals:** sums of the available per-test medians: **Total WIP** for the controlled backends, **Total** for references and external backends. Backlog never contributes. Empty Stable groups are shown as *Coming soon...* and have no defined total, ratio or mean. These totals do not represent an application benchmark. > - **Summaries:** `μ` = arithmetic mean, `Q₂` = median, `G` = geometric mean of the case ratios. Each case has equal weight. All four ratios use exactly the same measured cases on both sides: Go/C and Go/JS both cover all 37 measured Go cases. The full total of a reference table is not used as a denominator for a different set of cases. Very small reference times can produce large ratios. > - **Missing data:** `—` means unavailable or not applicable, never zero. Bounds (`< …`) are excluded from summaries. `n=a/b` indicates coverage: measured cases out of listed cases for a time total, or matched references out of measured cases for a ratio. Historical diagnostic measurements remain in the reference tables; their controlled-backend counterparts belong to unmeasured Backlog. > - **Display precision, in every table:** values ≥ 1 use two decimal places (`12.000045 → 12.00`); positive values < 1 keep two significant digits after leading zeros (`0.000045`, `0.009492 → 0.0095`). Zero is `0.00`. > - **Opaque inputs, in every table:** inputs must remain unknown to the optimizer at runtime. Algebraic simplification is allowed; substituting the driver’s known input is not. > - **Calculations:** use archived timings before display rounding, including for threshold checks. `≈` marks a fallback to published precision. ### Core stresstest benchmark results (pure computational) **Core tests (`src/`)** cover features common to all tested targets (`./bin/run`) #### JavaScript JS Benchmark | Hand-written PureScript

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Observe an intentional external alias mutation inside the real opaque count effect."""
import argparse
import hashlib
import json
import os
from pathlib import Path
import subprocess
import sys

def digest(path):
    return hashlib.sha256(Path(path).read_bytes()).hexdigest()

def main():
    parser=argparse.ArgumentParser();parser.add_argument('build',type=Path);parser.add_argument('proof',type=Path);args=parser.parse_args()
    proof=args.proof.resolve()
    generator=Path(__file__).with_name('record-input-proof.py')
    subprocess.run([sys.executable,str(generator),str(args.build),str(proof),'--prepare-only'],check=True,capture_output=True,text=True)
    manifest=json.loads((proof/'manifest.json').read_text())
    widths={'RecordSetSmall1000':2,'RecordSetMedium1000':8,'RecordSetLarge1000':16}
    inputs=[]
    for name,width in widths.items():
        fields=[list(range(1,width+1)),[2147483647 if i%2==0 else -2147483648 for i in range(width)]]
        for count in [0,1,7]:
            for values in fields:
                for layout in ['dictionary','map']:
                    inputs.append({'case':len(inputs),'name':name,'count':count,'fields':values,'layout':layout})
    (proof/'inputs.json').write_text(json.dumps(inputs,indent=2)+'\n')
    override=proof/'opaque-override.go';text=override.read_text()
    assert text.count('RecordAuditCalls++')==1
    text=text.replace('RecordAuditCalls++','RecordAuditCalls++\n        if RecordAuditCalls == 2 && RecordAuditMutation != nil { RecordAuditMutation() }')
    text+='\nvar RecordAuditMutation func()\n';override.write_text(text)
    original=next(iter(json.loads((proof/'overlay.json').read_text())['Replace']))
    import difflib
    (proof/'opaque-override.patch').write_text(''.join(difflib.unified_diff(Path(original).read_text().splitlines(True),text.splitlines(True),fromfile=original,tofile=str(override))))
    program=(proof/'main.go').read_text()
    old='action:=actions[input.Name];original:=record(input,prepared[input.Name]);unchanged(original,input)\n   for _,path:=range []string{"Apply","ffi_conversion","forced_fallback"}{'
    assert program.count(old)==1
    boundary=program.split('.RecordAuditInputs=',1)[0].split()[-1]
    replacement='''action:=actions[input.Name]
   for _,path:=range []string{"Apply","ffi_conversion","forced_fallback"}{
     original:=record(input,prepared[input.Name]);unchanged(original,input)
     alias:=original;mutations:=0
     BOUNDARY.RecordAuditMutation=func(){mutations++;mutateRecord(alias,string(rune('a'+len(input.Fields)-1)))}'''.replace('BOUNDARY',boundary)
    program=program.replace(old,replacement)
    oldcheck='unchanged(original,input)\n     fmt.Printf'
    assert program.count(oldcheck)==1
    program=program.replace(oldcheck,'''if mutations!=1{panic("alias mutation effect count")}
     changed:=input;changed.Fields=append([]int64{},input.Fields...);last:=len(changed.Fields)-1;changed.Fields[last]=int64(int32(changed.Fields[last]+17))
     unchanged(original,changed);unchanged(alias,changed)
     fmt.Printf''')
    program+='''
func mutateRecord(value r.Value,key string){
 switch value.Type {
 case r.TypeRecordData:
  data:=(*r.RecordData)(value.UnsafePtr);for i,label:=range data.Keys{if label==key{data.Vals[i]=r.Int(int64(int32(data.Vals[i].IntVal+17)));return}}
 case r.TypeRecord:
  data:=*(*map[string]r.Value)(value.UnsafePtr);data[key]=r.Int(int64(int32(data[key].IntVal+17)));return
 }
 panic("unexpected alias mutation representation")
}
'''
    (proof/'main.go').write_text(program)
    oracle=(proof/'oracle.mjs').read_text();assert oracle.count('let original=0;')==1
    oracle=oracle.replace('let original=0;','fields[fields.length-1]=(fields[fields.length-1]+17)|0;\n  let original=0;')
    (proof/'oracle.mjs').write_text(oracle)
    assert all(digest(k)==v for k,v in manifest['generated_source_sha256'].items())
    result=subprocess.run(manifest['command'],cwd=Path(manifest['build'])/'output',env={**os.environ,'GOWORK':'off'},text=True,capture_output=True,timeout=120)
    (proof/'stdout.txt').write_text(result.stdout);(proof/'stderr.txt').write_text(result.stderr);assert result.returncode==0,result.stderr
    expected=subprocess.check_output(['node',str(proof/'oracle.mjs'),str(proof/'inputs.json')],text=True);(proof/'expected.txt').write_text(expected);assert result.stdout==expected
    assert all(digest(k)==v for k,v in manifest['generated_source_sha256'].items());assert digest(Path(manifest['build'])/'benchmark')==manifest['binary_sha256']
    manifest.update(validated=True,input_variants=len(inputs),oracles=len(inputs)*3,record_representations=['dictionary','map'],counter_domain=[0,1,7],inputs_immutable=False,external_alias_mutation_observed_once=True,compiler_added_mutation=False,override_sha256=digest(override),mutation_delta=17)
    manifest['limitation']='A diagnostic overlay mutates the input through an alias inside opaqueValue when the count effect actually runs. Both the original boxed path and the new direct worker invoke that same effect body. The caller must observe this intentional external mutation once, before record projection and consumption; no mutation is added by the compiler. Benchmark/FFI sources and official generated builds remain unchanged.'
    manifest['artifact_sha256']={p.name:digest(p) for p in proof.iterdir() if p.is_file() and p.name!='manifest.json'}
    (proof/'manifest.json').write_text(json.dumps(manifest,indent=2)+'\n')
    print(f'{len(inputs)*3} alias-boundary controls passed; mutation occurs once inside the count effect.')

if __name__=='__main__':main()
